faqs.q: How long does a TPO roof last in West Orange?

runs.v: A TPO membrane lasts 7 to 20 years per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, with 15 to 25 years commonly cited in field practice. TPO fails most often at the welded seams, so a heat-welded, well-drained membrane reaches the longer end of the range, against EPDM at 15 to 25 years and BUR at 30 years per the InterNACHI chart.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a TPO roof in West Orange, NJ?

runs.v: New Jersey applies the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code (UCC) to roofing installations, and a building permit is mandatory when a commercial, multi-family, or attached TPO installation replaces or repairs more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7; that 25% rule is a permit threshold, not a rule that forces a full replacement, and work below it is ordinary maintenance. The ordinary-maintenance exemption for a detached one- or two-family reroof does not extend to a commercial building, so confirm with the West Orange construction office before work on a Main Street, Valley Road, Pleasant Valley Way, or Route 280 building.

faqs.q: Is TPO or PVC better for a West Orange commercial building?

runs.v: Both are heat-welded single-ply membranes, but PVC lasts 20 to 30 years and resists grease and chemicals, while TPO lasts 7 to 20 years and installs at a lower cost; the PVC figure traces to the Single Ply Roofing Industry (SPRI) and the TPO figure to the InterNACHI chart. PVC suits a restaurant exhaust roof along Main Street or Valley Road, while white TPO is the cost-effective reflective choice elsewhere.

faqs.q: Can TPO be installed over my existing West Orange commercial roof?

runs.v: A TPO recover installs the new membrane over a sound existing roof, but N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 prohibits a recover when the existing covering is water-soaked, is wood shake, slate, clay, cement, or asbestos-cement tile, or already carries 2 or more layers, so Newark Quality Roofing takes a core sample before specifying a recover over a tear-off.

faqs.q: Does TPO work on a historic landmark roof in West Orange?

runs.v: TPO works on a low-slope section of an older building, but a locally designated landmark or a property in a historic district can need extra review before a permit issues, and a private community such as Llewellyn Park may have its own rules for exterior work, so confirm with the West Orange construction office before roofing work begins.
